name: Mahru-Z
maker: Korea Institute of Science and Technology
def: KIST humanoid built for household chores, using three dimensional vision to recognise objects and operate appliances with its own hands and feet.
body: Mahru-Z was announced by the Cognitive Robotics Center at KIST in February 2010 as the fourth robot of the Mahru family, standing about 1.3 m tall and weighing around 55 kg. It walks with onboard balance control, recognises objects and people in three dimensions and was demonstrated putting fruit into a basket, tidying a table, loading a microwave and pressing appliance controls. The same laboratory built the Mahru-M mobile variant and used the family to study whole body imitation of motion captured from a human performer.
facts: Fourth generation of the KIST Mahru humanoid family
Demonstrated household chores including operating a microwave
specs: Three dimensional vision system, force sensing feet
Recognises objects and sequences chores from high level commands
